claims.text: Wear-induced dynamic amorphization and near-surface grain refinement are the primary governors of coupled HEA tribo-corrosion degradation.
The wear-induced microstructural transformation promotes formation of a more homogeneous and adherent passive oxide film.
The passive oxide film reduces friction by lowering interfacial shear strength.
The passive oxide film protects the HEA against chemical attack.
The proposed initial material is an additively manufactured, initially coarse-grained, single-phase HEA.
The proposed initial HEA has high phase stability.
The proposed initial HEA derives substantial strength from solution strengthening.
High strain rates during sliding generate extreme grain refinement and amorphization in the surface layer.
Grain boundaries in the dynamically refined layer provide fast diffusion paths for oxygen and alloying elements and thereby accelerate passive-film formation.
Dynamic refinement facilitates localized segregation of corrosion-inhibiting alloying species.
Ultra-nanocrystalline HEAs can exhibit inverse Hall-Petch softening.
A uniform, stable oxide film reduces mechanical wear through inverse Hall-Petch-related lowering of shear strength.
The coupled tribo-corrosion condition will produce lower-than-additive total degradation.
Wear rate under coupled tribo-corrosion will be reduced because of a low-shear amorphous surface layer.
Corrosion rate under sliding will be lower than for an otherwise matched, chemically exposed but unworked sample.
The beneficial mechanism should operate at moderate chloride concentrations that permit oxide-film formation.
Extremely aggressive environments can continuously disrupt the passive film and eliminate the predicted benefit.
The predicted benefit will fail when imposed shear is insufficient to induce the required near-surface transformation.
An ultra-high-vacuum or chemically inert wear baseline can help separate mechanical wear from effects involving reactive species and oxide films.
Mixed metal-oxide surface films can substantially affect HEA strength and deformation or wear resistance.
